patch.value: Release pipeline permits duplicate same-day production versions

Close the release-policy enforcement gap that allowed three 2026.7.24 tags and two npm publications. Remove the local same-day ordinal bypass, fail closed on legacy override attempts, require a single calendar version per UTC day, document same-tag partial-release recovery, and prove the invariant with unit, integration, workflow-contract, and isolated manual tests.

The release preparation pipeline cannot create an ordinal same-day production version; Any existing UTC-day release tag yields release_already_cut_today before mutation; Legacy same-day override requests fail closed with actionable same-tag recovery guidance; Release documentation explains retrying the existing tag after partial npm or GitHub failures

patch.value: Removed every same-day ordinal preparation path, bound explicit targets to the current UTC date before Git access, made today's tag guard unconditional, and changed blocker recovery to rerun the exact immutable tag workflow.
At most one production tag and npm version can be created per UTC day, and partial publication failures recover the existing tag without another version.

Legacy overrides, ordinal targets, and past/future explicit dates fail before Git inspection; an existing day tag skips preparation; blocker closure reruns/watches the exact Release run. Local/full hosted gates and two review rounds validate the behavior.
